quote: 11.2 Indemnification of AbbVie. Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless, from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]
rationale:
Article 11's architecture is sound and partly favourable: Section 11.2 gives us an express defend-and-indemnify duty from Harpoon running to AbbVie, its Affiliates and their personnel for Third Party Claims, and Sections 11.3, 11.4.1 and 11.4.4 supply notice, control of the defence and cooperation. Those four preferred elements are already met and we leave them untouched.

The operative scope, however, is not established on the rendered record: both 11.2 and 11.1 end "arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]". Nothing rendered confirms that Harpoon's indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, a Harpoon-caused data or confidentiality breach, or Harpoon's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and nothing confirms that our own 11.1 exposure stays narrow. The Section 7.4 cross-reference ("Subject to Section 11.2") is inference, not operative indemnity text, and Section 7.4 otherwise puts first-line defence of third-party patent claims on AbbVie at its own expense. Fallback is also unavailable: the procure/modify/replace and refund remedies appear nowhere, and there is no 3x-annual-fees super-cap in Article 11.

We therefore add the missing scope as short additions to the existing trigger lists rather than rewriting them. Operation 2 confirms Harpoon's indemnity covers Third Party Claims alleging that the Licensed Compounds, Licensed Products, Harpoon Patents or Harpoon Know-How infringe or misappropriate Third Party intellectual property, plus Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, Harpoon-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of our Confidential Information or data, and Harpoon's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Operation 1 confines our 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided materials, Information or content and AbbVie's breach of Applicable Law. Both are drafted as "without limiting"/limiting sentences so the redacted triggers are supplemented or capped rather than contradicted, and neither duplicates the 11.3/11.4 procedure. This is a scope-confirmation ask, not walk-away territory; if the unredacted triggers already carry this scope, the operations can be dropped.

rationale:
The Agreement contains no aggregate liability cap for either Party. Article 11 supplies mutual indemnities (Sections 11.1/11.2), a mutual all-caps exclusion of indirect and consequential damages with carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, breach of Article 9 or Section 5.8, and third-party indemnity pass-through (Section 11.5), and insurance minimums (Section 11.6). Searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed", "limitation of liability", "maximum liability", "no event shall", "liable", "damages" and "Losses" return no cap; the only "maximum aggregate" figures are Article 6 milestone payment ceilings, not liability limits. Both fallback cap elements are therefore absent from the operative text, so the clause the rule expects is missing.

We have inserted a single new Section 11.7 at the end of Article 11 stating a mutual cap — "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — at the fallback basis (no USD 1,000,000 floor is volunteered). Because the new cap would otherwise swallow currently unlimited exposures, the same sentence expressly places outside the cap each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 11, breaches of Article 9 (confidentiality) or Section 5.8 (Harpoon's exclusivity), and its fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence, mirroring the existing Section 11.5 exceptions. Placement at the end of Article 11 as Section 11.7 avoids renumbering Section 11.6 and creates no dangling cross-reference; Section 11.5 is left verbatim.

Note for the deal team: the cap is symmetric and preserves our recourse for indemnified and confidentiality claims, but it is a real change of risk allocation in a deal whose consideration is an upfront/option payment, Article 6 milestones and Net Sales royalties rather than recurring fees. If the business prefers to keep the mutually uncapped regime (which does not trigger any walk-away test), this edit can be dropped; if it is taken forward, we would also press to place AbbVie's Article 6 payment obligations and infringement of the other Party's intellectual property outside the cap, which is our preferred position.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: a single inserted Section 11.7 delivers a mutual cap on a 12-month fee basis with indemnification, confidentiality (Article 9), gross negligence and wilful misconduct expressly outside the cap. No level-complete element is left to the margin comment. Preferred fails on four elements: (i) no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor; (ii) no carve-out for breach of data protection/security obligations; (iii) no carve-out for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property; (iv) no statement that AbbVie's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. To move to preferred, amend 11.7 to read "...shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by AbbVie ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" and add the missing carve-outs plus "AbbVie's obligation to pay amounts due under Article 6 shall not be subject to this cap." Substantive defect in the cap basis even at fallback: "fees" is not a defined term in this Agreement and the consideration is an upfront/option payment, Article 6 milestones and Net Sales royalties. As drafted the cap could be read as near-zero in any 12-month window without a "fee" payment, making Harpoon's exposure to AbbVie illusory. Repair by using "all amounts paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement" (or an express reference to Article 6 payments) and, preferably, adding the USD 1,000,000 floor. Related repair: because 11.7 caps "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement", it is capable of being read against AbbVie's own retained Article 6 payment obligations. This is not a facial contradiction (caps and debt obligations customarily coexist), but the payment carve-out named above should be added to remove the ambiguity against retained royalty/milestone mechanics. Minimality holds: one concise new section at the end of Article 11, Section 11.5 left verbatim, no renumbering of 11.6, no survival tail, procedure or extra damages categories. The fraud and Section 5.8 carve-outs are not gratuitous extras — they mirror retained Section 11.5(A)-(B) and are needed so the new cap does not swallow exposures that are presently uncapped. Intent preserved: the mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, the mutual indemnities, the insurance minimums and the Article 6 payment ceilings survive; the new cross-references (Article 9, Section 5.8, Article 11) all resolve and no dangling reference is created. Commercial caution for the deal team (consistent with the drafter's note): the pre-existing regime is mutually uncapped, which is not a walk-away outcome and preserves AbbVie's full recourse against Harpoon. Introducing any cap trades that recourse away, so this edit should be raised only if the business wants symmetry; severity is downgraded accordingly.
